conf.description: zos-racf resource-access, format syslog-leef: structural LEEF header split only (vendor/product/version/eventId are wire-format-guaranteed positions) -- the zSecure interface's named attribute list cannot be mapped to ECS because its attribute names are unpublished and no captured sample exists; the attribute blob and _raw are both retained verbatim as the forensic backstop for this deliberately incomplete pipeline.

conf.comment: zos-racf/resource-access/syslog-leef. The work order's own parsing.notes say the class/name split and the requested-versus-granted authority pair 'have to be reconstructed from the LEEF attributes, whose names are set by the zSecure interface and are not published; build against a captured sample.' Guessing a delimiter or attribute-name mapping here would be exactly the silent-failure risk the brief warns hardest about, so this pipeline only extracts what the LEEF spec itself guarantees regardless of site config -- the 5 pipe-delimited header fields -- and preserves the full attribute blob unparsed on racf.access.leef_attributes_raw plus _raw. No ECS mapping, no event.outcome/event.action, and no volume shaping are implemented; see README for the full gap list. This is intentionally a skeleton pending a real sample, not a finished pipeline.

functions.description: document why ECS mapping was deliberately not attempted for the named LEEF attributes

split the 5 pipe-delimited LEEF header fields plus the trailing attribute blob (tolerates a leading syslog envelope since unanchored) -- this part of the LEEF spec is guaranteed regardless of the site's zSecure attribute naming

copy the header-derived fields and the unparsed attribute blob to their custom homes; leef_event_id is kept raw rather than guessed onto event.action since this dataset's eventId semantics are not confirmed (unlike the fireeye family's analogous by-analogy mapping, there is no sibling RACF LEEF pipeline here to anchor that guess)

delete the now-consumed temporary header/attribute-blob fields; _raw is deliberately kept as the only complete record of the site's actual named attributes until a captured sample allows a full mapping
